sections.what_happened: Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Ja'bari told Al Jazeera about 2,200 Palestinians have been forced from their homes in al-Jalda and Ein Deir Bahha since Friday's raids; residents can neither enter nor leave Hebron; the Ibrahimi Mosque staff were removed, prayers banned and gates closed. AP confirms Israel imposed widespread closures and displaced people across Hebron on Saturday after gunmen killed two soldiers Friday; WAFA says troops forced dozens from homes in some neighbourhoods Saturday and closed all entrances/roads; the Israeli army did not respond to AP questions about Saturday's evacuations. Netanyahu, visiting the area, vowed: 'We will clear out the residents, go house to house, take out the weapons and all the infrastructure of terror,' applying the refugee-camp model to the Hebron neighbourhood. Activist Issa Amro (attributed, single source) says nearly 800,000 in the governorate are under siege and nearly 1,000 families are locked inside homes. NOTE on scope: WAFA's 'dozens' is a Saturday-morning neighbourhood count; the mayor's 2,200 is the cumulative al-Jalda/Ein Deir Bahha figure -- not a contradiction.
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera liveblog (mayor interview + activist account) and AP Saturday report (closures, displacement, WAFA count) converge on the operation's scale; IDF statement provides the Israeli framing.
sections.what_disputed: IDF: the operation is 'targeted and limited'; residents in operating areas may leave through three designated exit points after questioning and security screening; the army says it is searching for weapons and suspects after two soldiers were killed and others wounded. Netanyahu frames the measures as counterterrorism ahead of the Oct 27 election; Palestinian officials call it collective punishment.
sections.why_matters: 2,200 people out of their homes -- and the prime minister promising house-to-house clearing days before an election.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261024-1700-06 (Hebron operation, day 2) -- mayor puts displaced at about 2,200; AP confirms Saturday closures; Netanyahu vows house-to-house clearing

totw_analysis: Our read: 2,200 people out of their homes -- and the prime minister promising house-to-house clearing days before an election. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Evacuation for security versus forced displacement as collective punishment -- and is the timing about the Oct 27 election?
